summary: First live bench of mypintusan's OSDP Secure Channel (tools/fleetbench/bench_pintusan_securechannel.py, 18 checks), item 1 of a new hardening register for the app that physically opens doors, which had exactly one live bench before this. Secure Channel is the only thing standing between a screwdriver and a building on an RS-485 bus, and its two security-critical fault-table rows - a reader that refuses the handshake, and a session that drops mid-conversation - had never actually been driven against a live appliance: tools/osdp-sim's refuse-sc/no-sc/wrong-key scenarios presented no card at all, so they could show a session being refused but not what a badge does next, which is the half of 'must fail closed' that matters. The simulator now runs a card loop on all three so that claim can actually be demonstrated. Each bench episode is a fresh boot, because a reader's key and its RequireSecureChannel policy are seeded from config on first boot only and there is no API to change either afterwards. TWO REAL DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED. (1) A session that established and then DROPPED mid-conversation left the door granting on cleartext: infra/access/osdp/bus.go's secureChannelLost only re-announced the downgrade from StatusSecuring (a handshake that never came up), so a reader already StatusOnline when its session died produced no event and every consumer kept the SecureSession:true it was told at handshake, permanently. Measured against the simulator's sc-drop scenario, a door requiring an encrypted session went on granting badges on a reader whose session had died - precisely the RS-485 tap this mechanism exists to defeat. Fixed by re-announcing from StatusOnline too. (2) A critical or perimeter door created without mentioning Secure Channel did not require one: entities/door.go's own field comment has always said RequireSecureChannel 'defaults on for perimeter and critical', but the create handler passed the request body's boolean straight through while every neighbouring field (UnlockSeconds, HeldOpenSeconds, OfflinePolicy) got a real default. Measured live, a card on a plaintext reader opened a critical door. Fixed with a new entities.SecureChannelDefault(class) function and turning the create request's field into a *bool so an explicit false is distinguishable from silence; this mattered more than an ordinary defaulting bug because there is no PUT /api/doors, so a door created with the wrong policy kept it for good. Two new unit tests cover the default in apps/mypintusan/services/decision_test.go. PROVEN GOOD AND UNCHANGED: a healthy secure session grants; no-sc and refuse-sc both deny with the specific reason secure-channel-failed rather than a vaguer one; a door that does not require SC still works with a reader that cannot do it; a key mismatch never becomes a cleartext session and is alarmed. A FEATURE GAP WAS FOUND AND REPORTED, NOT BUILT: Reader.ScbkState is written once at creation as 'default' and never updated - ScbkRekeyed/ScbkFailed are declared in entities/reader.go and assigned nowhere, and although infra/access/osdp already answers a PDCAP capability request and carries the result as Event.DefaultKey/DefaultKeySession, nothing in apps/mypintusan reads either field, so a reader still on the factory default key is never capped to interior-only as the design intends. 18/18 checks pass with the fixes; 13/18 against the unfixed app.
compatibility: Backward-compatible for every legitimate use; no schema or config change. Behavioural fix, not a new feature: a reader whose established Secure Channel session drops mid-conversation on a door that requires one is now correctly taken out of service and alarmed instead of continuing to grant on a downgraded, unencrypted link - any install relying on the old (unintended) behaviour was relying on a security hole. A door created via POST /api/doors that omits requireSecureChannel now inherits the documented class default (on for perimeter/critical, off for interior) instead of silently getting none; a caller that explicitly sends requireSecureChannel:false is unaffected, since that is now distinguishable from omission. Existing doors already created with the old silent-false behaviour are NOT retroactively changed - there is no PUT /api/doors, so any perimeter/critical door provisioned before this fix should be checked and, if needed, recreated with the field explicit. Scope is `infra` rather than `mypintusan`: mypintusan has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map yet, and an unknown scope token hard-fails the release run.
